name: Mountain Sunday

attributes.attribute: the last Sunday of July, a climb kept from the feast of Lughnasa
the Celtic harvest feast that opened the season on August 1
a holy peak in the west of Ireland climbed on that Sunday

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mountain Sunday is a later form of the feast of Lughnasa. It comes on the last Sunday of July. On that day the faithful climb a high hill, a rite that began with the old Celtic harvest feast. That feast, which the Celts called Lughnasa, opened the harvest on August 1. To climb a high place at Lughnasa was old Celtic custom. The best known climb today is to the peak of Croagh Patrick in the west of Ireland. The holy mount holds the old feast alive in a new Christian rite. The climb keeps a link to the summer feast of the first day of August.
